output.brief: I collected no further evidence, so this is provisional. The strongest signal is that Callerby's own tower crane and frame crew left Corran Valley for Kestrel from October 2025 to April 2026. Your site superintendent, the project director and Halden all confirm it. Meanwhile steel for the upper levels was on site, and the drafted claim attributes the full 26 weeks to Halden. It rests on an RFI log "created" date and on Callerby's own programme updates, and the claims consultant earns 6% of whatever is recovered. I would not submit the claim as drafted, because it is likely to fail and could damage your credibility. I would not concede everything yet either. Before 1 December, get an independent delay analysis. It should use the RFI platform's audit timestamps, the architect's change order register, the daily site diaries and the crane ledger, to separate Halden-caused delay from Callerby's own. Do not discipline the superintendent. He answered truthfully, and punishing him would discourage people from reporting problems. Do not suspend the incentive scheme yet. Whether it drove the crane move is not established. Review how crane and crew moves between projects get approved. Confidence is moderate to low until the records are checked.
